items.content_excerpt: $CVNA $NVDA $PLTR $DELL $SPCX Everyone is cheering AI integration into business, manufacturing, research, inventions, and service industries. I get it: AI can boost productivity, increase margins, and send corporate earnings soaring. The rich get richer while average workers risk losing their livelihoods. But at what cost to society? If tens of millions lose their jobs and income, tax revenues will fall while government deficits and demands for assistance rise. Here’s the million-dollar question: WHO WILL BUY ALL THOSE CORPORATIONS’ PRODUCTS, AND WITH WHAT MONEY? No job means no income, limited credit, and potentially no purchasing power. People still need to pay rent or mortgages, buy groceries, cover utilities, healthcare, childcare, and other necessities. What happens to corporate earnings when consumers can no longer afford their products? And what happens to those insane stock market valuations when growth and profits fail to meet expectations? DO YOU SEE THE CONTRADICTION?

That is this swing setup in plain terms. AMD closed Tuesday at 534.74 dollars after touching 524.60, then buyers pushed it to about 551 in after hours trading, which tells you that low held for now and sellers lost some grip. With earnings coming on November 3, the run into that date is the window, and holding above that low is what keeps this call side read honest. P.S. Watch 570 on the way up. It was the closing level on October 14, and a close above it would open the road toward 605.

items.content_excerpt: $SPCX Elon responds on $SPCX & $TSLA merger: "Both Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees at the request of shareholders. Because I'm a conflicted party I can't be in on these discussions. I don't think we should assume that a merger is a certainty. Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes. items.title: Amazon is radically changing its hardware procurement strategy, committing to receive billions of dollars in Nvidia AI servers before its da
items.content_excerpt: Amazon is radically changing its hardware procurement strategy, committing to receive billions of dollars in Nvidia AI servers before its data centers have enough electricity to operate them. According to internal emails obtained by Business Insider, Amazon launched an “Early Rack Receipt” program to accept approximately $5B in Nvidia GB300 server racks at U.S. facilities, with plans to take delivery of another $3B in additional hardware monthly. The equipment is reportedly being stored in intermediary warehouses because several AWS data centers lack sufficient power capacity, leaving some GPUs idle. This creates a significant financial burden, as Amazon must commit capital to hardware before it can generate cloud revenue. Previously, the company generally took ownership and recorded expenses when server racks reached operational data centers. $AMZN $NVDA

items.content_excerpt: $META Quiz time 😂 Here’s the classic tricky hotel room question: Three friends check into a hotel. The room costs $30, so each person pays $10. Later, the hotel manager realizes the room should have cost only $25. He gives the bellboy $5 to return to the three friends. On the way, the bellboy realizes $5 can't be divided equally among three people, so he keeps $2.X for himself and gives each friend $1.X back. Now, each friend has paid $9, meaning the three friends paid a total of $27. The bellboy kept $2. $27 + $2.X = $29. 🤔 Where did the missing $1.X go?

It fully exited Constellation Brands and reduced holdings in Bank of America, Chubb and Nucor. DO YOU SEE THE CONTRADICTION?

items.content_excerpt: $NFLX Netflix investors quiz... Don't open the comments until you yourself figure out the answer first. Three friends check into a hotel. The room costs $30, so each person pays $10. Later, the hotel manager realizes the room should have cost only $25. He gives the bellboy $5 to return to the three friends. On the way, the bellboy realizes $5 can't be divided equally among three people, so he keeps $2 for himself and gives each friend $1 back. Now, each friend has paid $9, meaning the three friends paid a total of $27. The bellboy kept $2. $27 + $2 = $29. 🤔 Where did the missing $1 go?

items.content_excerpt: $BA the FAA certified the 737 MAX 10 yesterday, October twentieth. About forty MAX 7s and MAX 10s were sitting in inventory as of June, and by end of August that had grown to roughly one hundred sixteen finished narrowbodies across the industry, mostly those two variants needing post-production rework before they could move. As for the next thirty days, essentially zero MAX 10s. Boeing is saying deliveries begin in the coming months, with WestJet as launch customer targeted for early next year, northern spring 2027. Two things still stand between the type certificate and a handover. First, Transport Canada and EASA certification, which Boeing’s Mike Sinnett called probably a couple more months. items.title: $UVIX got another scalp bear wide for a few %. I’ve said this many times, but due to how $VIX and x2 leverage actually function this will al
items.content_excerpt: $UVIX got another scalp bear wide for a few %. I’ve said this many times, but due to how $VIX and x2 leverage actually function this will always have mathematical downside bias long term. Easiest way to think of it is like this Ticker A is base ticker and ticker B2 is the x2 mover. For ease of example pretend both are $10 A goes up 20%, so it’s at $12 and B2 is at $14 due to going 40%. Both tickers then go down 20% next day. A then goes 9.60 (12 * .8) but B drops down to 8.4 when it loses 40% (14 * .6) Basically the exact same movement that led ticker A with only a 4% drop of initial value cost the leveraged ticker 16%. This will ALWAYS drops harder than it rises on proportionate move

items.title: General Motors shares plunged on Tuesday after the automaker lowered its full-year profit expectations and announced plans to temporarily pa
items.content_excerpt: General Motors shares plunged on Tuesday after the automaker lowered its full-year profit expectations and announced plans to temporarily pause production at some truck facilities, raising concerns about vehicle output and earnings. The stock fell sharply, with losses reaching 8.87%, putting it on track for its worst single-day decline since July 22, 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The revised outlook suggests that production adjustments could reduce vehicle availability in the near term and weigh on overall profitability. The announcement comes despite GM reporting higher automotive revenue for the September quarter compared with the same period last year, even though it sold fewer vehicles. Investors are focusing on whether the planned production pauses will affect deliveries, factory utilization and the company’s ability to meet its financial targets. $GM

$UVIX got another scalp bear wide for a few %. I’ve said this many times, but due to how $VIX and x2 leverage actually function this will always have mathematical downside bias long term. Easiest way to think of it is like this Ticker A is base ticker and ticker B2 is the x2 mover. For ease of example pretend both are $10 A goes up 20%, so it’s at $12 and B2 is at $14 due to going 40%. Both tickers then go down 20% next day. A then goes 9.60 (12 * .8) but B drops down to 8.4 when it loses 40% (14 * .6) Basically the exact same movement that led ticker A with only a 4% drop of initial value cost the leveraged ticker 16%. This will ALWAYS drops harder than it rises on proportionate move

The revised outlook suggests that production adjustments could reduce vehicle availability in the near term and weigh on overall profitability. The announcement comes despite GM reporting higher automotive revenue for the September quarter compared with the same period last year, even though it sold fewer vehicles.
